Lots of these could be forward declared instead. (besides control.h and code_editor.h probably).
And vector should already be transitively included.

```suggestion
				current->goto_line_centered(p_line);
```
This should go to the line centered.

```suggestion
	LocalVector<String> types = { "Script", "JSON" };
```
Lists are avoided where possible, this one can be a LocalVector.

This code is for TextFiles only, real resources are handled elsewhere.
So if current isn't TextEditorBase, then it should do nothing or fail instead of only setting the path (below this condition).
Why is this only for TextEditorBase?
This changes the order, but the order is important, it should be enabled before going to the tab.
This check shouldn't be removed.
The `p_` generally indicates that it is a parameter, this could be `file_menu_popup` or something, though it isn't really needed. Accessing through `get_popup()` repeatedly is pretty common.
This isn't used, if its needed in the future it can be added then.

This only checks TextEditorBase for scripts, but other places like `_update_history_pos` use scripts from any ScriptEditorBase source, is there a reason for this?
Not that it really matters since there is no non-text script editor.
`_test_script_times_on_disk` could change the contents of the text, so `goto_line` should stay after it.
Calling this in the loop means it needs to be re evaluated each time, it should be cached outside the loop.

```suggestion
	// TODO: This should be combined with the search_menu in TextEditorBase.
```
I agree with this, though I'm not sure if we need to add a TODO here.

It's fine to combine the `p_can_fold` and `p_is_folded` parameters, but the value passed in should be `can_fold || is_folded`, like in `ScriptTextEditor`.
Same with the other use below.
This is for breakpoints, it cannot use the bookmarks function.
The signals should be emitted after the validation, not before.
This needs to check `editor_enabled` like ScriptTextEditor did it, or it reintroduces the issue fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84907

`_load_theme_settings()` is being called twice, in `_enable_code_editor()` and then in `TextEditorBase::enable_editor()`. Instead of adding this check to prevent it from running twice, `_enable_code_editor()` can just not call it.
If I am understanding this right.
Why are the menus created on ready?

The reason for these manual deletes is when the node is created but not added as a child, it doesn't get deleted automatically. (`add_submenu_node_item` adds as child too).
I think all of these are added as child (on ready for most, and `edit_hb` is always added in `edit()`, `code_editor` is always added by inherited classes for some reason), so none of them should be deleted here. 
When closing the editor, it looks like it is crashing instead of exiting cleanly, likely because of this.

Same with warnings_panel below.

I have been working on a separate PR to remove `editor_enabled`, so this kind of thing won't be needed in the future for ScriptTextEditor.

ScriptTextEditor should probably fail if it is not given a Script, instead of silently accepting any resource.

So the function is called after being overwritten by the subclass. When called in the constructor this is not possible from what I found

Hmmm don't know how this happened, I tried to always use the most general class possible. Will change this for consistency

Actually now that I think about it I am not sure why I changed this, it must have been either that there was an error or I thought it should be excluded from the visual editor (for whatever reason). I think I will just test the original version again and revert it if there are no problems
